comment: EXT-9 deliverable records: recognition, and the input/interim/output roles derived from them. A cross-surface contract like conformance/rooms-entry.json, and for the same reason - TWO implementations already compute these roles from the same record and must not disagree. services/src/rooms/dossier.ts (roleOf) decides which files a dossier keeps the BYTES of; app/src/files.ts (classify) decides what a room's files panel shows under Accepted. A file the panel calls Accepted and the dossier calls interim would mean the thing on screen is not the thing that was kept. THE FIXTURE IS THE AUTHORITY: when a test against it fails, fix the implementation; when the fixture is believed wrong, change it deliberately and update both sides together.
spec: EXT-9-deliverables.md (2. the records, 3. roles derived, 4. recognition)

recognition.comment: Matching is against the FIRST LINE only, and everything else is prose with no effect. That is normative, not an implementation shortcut: a record is mostly conversation, and a reader that inferred job state from prose would be guessing - a guess that silently satisfies a requirement is worse than having no requirement.

cases.name: claim with a dependency edge
cases.comment: `against:` is the job's edge, recorded after the fact rather than declared in advance.
cases.body:
DELIVERABLE · revision · @ v2 · ref: mesh:rooms:r1/drive/d2
against: review @ r1

Rewritten to answer the review.

cases.name: claim with no ref
cases.comment: Legal, and weaker. A claim naming no bytes cannot be checked against a digest; it parses so that a record made before a drive was reachable is still readable.

cases.name: acceptance
cases.body:
ACCEPTED · deliverable: revision @ v2
Good to ship.

cases.name: rejection carries its reason
cases.body:
REJECTED · deliverable: draft @ v1
reason: no skip condition, so it will be run out of habit

expected.name: draft
expected.reason: no skip condition, so it will be run out of habit

cases.name: prose is not a record
cases.body: I'll post the DELIVERABLE · draft · @ v1 line once the file is up.

cases.name: a record buried below the first line is not a record
cases.comment: First-line-only is what makes quoting a record safe. Without it, an agent repeating someone else's claim back to them would post it a second time under its own signature.
cases.body:
Quoting you:
DELIVERABLE · draft · @ v1 · ref: mesh:rooms:r1/drive/d1

cases.name: ordinary conversation
cases.body: Reading it now. Give me a few minutes.

roles.comment: Given a drive listing and a record, every file gets exactly one role. Nothing is stored and nobody files anything; a file's role can change later because the record said something new about it.

cases.name: a full job: brought in, superseded, accepted
record: Here is the brief I already had.

DELIVERABLE · review · @ r1 · ref: r/rev
against: draft @ v1

DELIVERABLE · revision · @ v2 · ref: r/d2
against: review @ r1

cases.name: a rejected version is interim, not an output
cases.comment: REJECTED does not make a file an input either: it WAS claimed as a deliverable, and demoting it to 'somebody brought this' would file a refused draft next to a contributed reference.
record:
REJECTED · deliverable: draft @ v1
reason: missing the skip condition

cases.name: a claim without a ref matches on name and version
an exact ref beats a name that also matches
cases.comment: A ref names one object; a name and version is a description two files can answer to. Resolving a precise claim by a guess is worse than not resolving it.

cases.name: a room that claims nothing has only inputs
cases.comment: The truthful answer for an ordinary conversation with files in it, and the reason a room needs no folders to be legible.
